newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower, Apr expires at $1.805.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower, Apr expires at $1.805.

text.p: NYMEX April Hub natgas expired 3.5 cents lower at $1.805 per mmBtu after some late shortcovering pushed it to as high as $1.835, industry sources said.
May also settled down 3.5 cents at $1.841 in another range-bound session. Other deferreds were marginally softer.

"It should be even quieter than normal over the next few days. The market is soft but not totally falling apart. I don't see anything that's going to drive it (May) ," one trader said, adding he expected the trading range to remain tight through the Easter holiday.

Technically, traders said there was minor support in May at today's low of $1.825, and then at $1.78 and $1.68. Resistance was seen at $1.90, and then at Thursday's high of $1.97. Further resistance was pegged at $2.04-2.05.

With moderate temperatures expected to cover most of the U.S. this week, some traders were doubtful May will be able to hold support, citing ample storage supplies in the East as another bearish fundamental.
However, well above-normal temperatures are expected to return to the Southwest by week's end, which will likely boost air-conditioning demand.
Most traders agreed that May trading would be off to a slow start until active storage injections get underway and clearer signals surface from the cash market.
NYMEX's 12-month strip fell 1.1 cents to $2.045 as an estimated 67,963 Hub contracts traded as of 1525 EST. Open interest for March 21 fell 790 to 175,355.

Despite the softer move in futures, Gulf cash prices for Tuesday were little changed at $1.85-1.88 at the Henry Hub. April prices at the hub mirrored futures at $1.78-1.80. Swing prices on the Midcontinent pipes were also steady in the low-to-mid $1.70s, while April was talked in the high-$1.60s to low-$1.70s. At the New York city-gate, swing prices were about five cents lower at $2.15-2.18, while April 1 was talked around $2.10.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded.
On the KCBT, April settled unchanged at $1.68 ahead of its expiry on Tuesday. Deferreds finished flat to three cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by one cent to 12.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices in the Permian basin were mostly steady in the high-$1.60s to low-$1.70s. April 1 deals were reported done in the low-$1.60s, up more than five cents from March indices.
